headline: Bypass matching nodes without advancing past the new neighbor
statement: Remove every node whose value equals val from a singly linked list and return the resulting head. Reuse the original surviving nodes in their original order, without changing their values.
intuition: A pointer to the predecessor can remove its next node without moving itself. This is essential for consecutive matching nodes: after deletion the next neighbor must be checked again.
approach: Place a dummy before head and set prev to dummy.
While prev.next exists, bypass it when its value equals val.
Advance prev only when the next node is retained.
correctness: The retained prefix ending at prev contains no forbidden value. Removing a matching next node leaves this prefix unchanged; retaining a nonmatching next node extends it by one valid node. Each step consumes one unprocessed node, so the final list contains exactly the original nonmatching nodes in their original order.
bruteForce: Copy every nonmatching value into a new list, which allocates O(n) nodes instead of modifying existing links.

complexity.explanation: Every original node is examined once; only a dummy and predecessor pointer are needed.

pitfalls: Do not advance prev after a deletion.
A dummy handles consecutive removals from the head.
An empty or fully removed list returns None.
